text: In today's digital world, anyone can publish a story online within seconds, which means news spreads faster than ever before. Unfortunately, this also makes it easier for misinformation to reach a huge audience. Sometimes false stories are shared by accident, but disinformation is created deliberately to mislead people for political or financial reasons. A dramatic headline can exaggerate the truth, and a single unverified claim can distort how people understand an event. Because so many websites publish content without checking their source, readers are becoming increasingly skeptical of what they read online. Professional journalists are trained to fact-check information and only report facts they can verify, but not every website follows the same standards. As a result, it is often difficult to know which source is credible and which one is not reliable. If people do not learn to think critically, misinformation can have a serious impact on elections, health decisions, and public trust. Experts suggest checking several sources, looking for the original claim, and asking whether a story seems too extreme to be accurate before sharing it with others.
